# 2 Baruch Chapter 28 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 28 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 28:1 — "seal of that time / mark of that era"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-seal-of-that-time" | Literal: Syriac hatma = seal/stamp |
| LOGOS | "the seal of that period" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "the mark of that era" | Substitutes "mark" and "era" for modern readability |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS "the seal of that period." "Seal" preserves the Syriac term's sense of an official divine stamp or certification. "Mark" is weaker.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 28:5 — "gone forth / left / departed"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-will-go-forth out-of-this-world" | Literal Syriac verb of departing/going out |
| LOGOS | "they will have gone forth from this world" | Perfect aspect — they depart before the tribulation |
| PNEUMA | "they will already have left this world" | Paraphrase with "already" emphasizing priority |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "will have gone forth from this world." The perfect aspect is critical here — the righteous die before the tribulation, not during it. PNEUMA's "already" adds the same sense but less precisely.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Aspect preserved.

---

## 28:7 — "Anointed One / Messiah"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Anointed-One" | Translates Syriac meshicha literally |
| LOGOS | "the Anointed One" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the Anointed One" | Same — unusual consensus |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three agree: "the Anointed One." No divergence.

**Status:** Consensus. No divergence.

---

## 28:7 — "will begin to be revealed / will be revealed"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-begin to-be-revealed" | Preserves the Syriac inceptive aspect (sha-ra d-nethgale) |
| LOGOS | "will begin to be revealed" | Preserves inceptive |
| PNEUMA | "will be revealed" | Drops the inceptive aspect |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "will begin to be revealed" (EMET/LOGOS). The Syriac clearly uses an inceptive construction — the revealing is a process that begins, not a single moment. This is theologically significant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Aspect preserved.

---
